procedure_text: WO 99/06339 discloses a process for preparing substituted benzyl bromides by brominating the corresponding methyl aromatics in the presence of azocarboxylic esters or azonitriles and in the presence of an oxidizing agent. In this case, one substituent is electronegative and is from the group fluorine, chlorine, bromine, alkoxycarbonyl, cyano and nitro. Disadvantages of this process are the use of an additional oxidizing agent and the not always satisfactory yields.
procedure_summary: A cited earlier international application discloses the side chain bromination of methyl aromatics carrying an electronegative substituent, run in the presence of azocarboxylic esters or azonitriles together with an oxidizing agent, to give substituted benzyl bromides. The patent objects to the extra oxidant and to yields it calls not always satisfactory.

The one judgement call is the Houben-Weyl sentence on line 55, 'Bromomethyl aromatics may in principle be prepared from the corresponding methyl aromatics by side chain bromination; on this subject, cf. Houben-Weyl, Vol. 5, page 331 ff. (1960)'. This pass weighed it again and reached the same view as the first pass and as A0: it is a TEXTBOOK CITATION and not a fourth transformation. Four reasons. It discloses no process, only that something may in principle be done. Its citation form is 'cf.' pointing at a handbook chapter, not the 'discloses a process' and 'describes the preparation' with which this same paragraph introduces the two disclosures that do get records. Its subject is the reaction type in general, with no substrate, no brominating agent, no solvent and no conditions, so a record built from it would restate Step 1's transformation with strictly less content in it. An extractor that emits a fourth record for the Houben-Weyl sentence is making a defensible reading and not an obvious error, and that is worth recording rather than settling.
